entries.title: Embedded Private Key Material
entries.description: The checked source contains a private-key block. Determine whether the key is active, a test fixture, or publicly distributed material.
entries.impact: An exposed active private key may allow impersonation, unauthorized signatures, or decryption where the corresponding protocol and key usage permit it.
entries.remediation: Remove active private keys from source and distributed artifacts. Revoke or rotate exposed keys, and store replacements in a restricted key-management service.

entries.title: Credentials In Connection URL
entries.description: A connection URL or authorization header embeds credential material directly in the checked source.
entries.impact: Anyone who can read the source, build artifacts, or copied configuration may recover active credentials and access the associated service with the credential owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation: Remove embedded credentials and load them from an approved secret store. Rotate exposed active credentials and restrict their privileges and lifetime.

entries.title: Unsigned JWT Algorithm Selection
entries.description: JWT configuration or processing explicitly selects an unsigned algorithm.
entries.impact: If unsigned tokens are accepted as authenticated claims, an attacker may forge identity, roles, or other trusted claims and gain unauthorized access.
entries.remediation: Require signature verification with a fixed allowlist of approved algorithms and trusted keys. Reject unsigned tokens and validate issuer, audience, and expiry.

entries.title: TLS Verification Disabled By Environment
entries.description: The checked code or configuration bypasses a certificate, hostname, or server-trust decision. Resolve the effective callback and build configuration before confirming a production bypass.
entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.
entries.remediation: Restore platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Reject invalid server trust, remove permissive callbacks and environment overrides from production, and use properly configured test trust stores for development.

entries.title: Sensitive Data In Logcat Output
entries.remediation: Remove or redact sensitive values before logging. Disable verbose payload and shell tracing in production, restrict log access, and rotate active credentials that have already been exposed.
entries.description: Diagnostic output or execution tracing includes values that may contain credentials, tokens, or private user data.
entries.impact: Sensitive values written to logs may be recovered by log readers, telemetry operators, or other parties with access to collected diagnostics, enabling account misuse or disclosure of private data.

entries.title: Wildcard CORS Annotation Or Origin Setting
entries.description: An origin policy accepts a wildcard for browser requests or WebView messaging. Identify the resources or native operations accessible through this policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted website may read protected responses or invoke privileged message handlers if the effective origin policy admits it and the resource or handler lacks the required independent access controls.
entries.remediation: Allow only the exact trusted origins required by the feature. Authenticate and authorize each operation independently; validate message origin and content before invoking native functionality.

entries.title: Wildcard CORS Annotation Or Origin Setting
entries.description: An origin policy accepts a wildcard for browser requests or WebView messaging. Identify the resources or native operations accessible through this policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted website may read protected responses or invoke privileged message handlers if the effective origin policy admits it and the resource or handler lacks the required independent access controls.
entries.remediation: Allow only the exact trusted origins required by the feature. Authenticate and authorize each operation independently; validate message origin and content before invoking native functionality.

entries.title: Wildcard CORS Annotation Or Origin Setting
entries.description: An origin policy accepts a wildcard for browser requests or WebView messaging. Identify the resources or native operations accessible through this policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted website may read protected responses or invoke privileged message handlers if the effective origin policy admits it and the resource or handler lacks the required independent access controls.
entries.remediation: Allow only the exact trusted origins required by the feature. Authenticate and authorize each operation independently; validate message origin and content before invoking native functionality.

entries.title: Route Prefix Without File-Level Authorization Marker
entries.description: A route declaration has no recognized authorization marker in the checked file. Global policies, middleware, or inherited controllers may still enforce access.
entries.impact: If no effective access policy protects a sensitive route, an unauthenticated or unauthorized caller may read protected data or perform restricted actions.
entries.remediation: Resolve global, inherited, and endpoint authorization policies. Apply an explicit policy to sensitive routes and test both anonymous access and access by users lacking the required role.

entries.title: Command Execution With External Input Markers
entries.description: The checked code invokes a command or shell execution API. Trace command construction and argument values to determine whether external input can influence execution.
entries.impact: If an attacker can alter executable selection or shell syntax, commands may run with the application’s privileges, exposing data, modifying files, or disrupting service.
entries.remediation: Use a fixed executable and a separate argument array without a shell. Allowlist permitted operations and validate each argument according to the invoked program’s semantics.

entries.title: User-Installed Certificates Trusted
entries.remediation: Limit user-installed trust anchors to justified development or managed-device scenarios. Keep debug overrides out of release builds and verify the selected domain trust policy.
entries.description: A network-security configuration includes user-installed certificate authorities in its trust anchors. Resolve debug overrides and domain-specific policies.
entries.impact: A party able to install a trusted certificate on the device may intercept affected connections if that certificate is accepted by the effective production trust policy.

entries.title: Certificate Pinning Override Enabled
entries.remediation: Remove pin overrides from production trust configurations unless explicitly required by the threat model. Verify the effective trust anchors and pin policy for each sensitive endpoint.
entries.description: A trust configuration allows a certificate source to override configured certificate pins.
entries.impact: Connections may accept certificates outside the intended pin set, allowing interception by a party controlling an accepted certificate authority when pinning was intended to provide an additional trust boundary.

entries.title: WebView Remote Debugging Enabled
entries.remediation: Enable WebView inspection only in verified development builds. Disable it in distributed releases and verify the setting in the final application artifact.
entries.description: WebView remote debugging or inspection is explicitly enabled. Determine whether the setting reaches a distributed production build.
entries.impact: A party with access to the platform’s debugging interface may inspect page content, extract session data, or execute scripts in the application’s WebView when production debugging remains accessible.

entries.title: WebView Mixed Content Allowed
entries.remediation: Use HTTPS with normal certificate validation. Remove unnecessary transport exceptions, keep any unavoidable exception narrowly scoped, and avoid sending credentials or loading executable content over cleartext connections.
entries.description: The effective transport policy may permit insecure HTTP content or relax transport protections for a WebView, media request, domain, or application.
entries.impact: A network attacker may read or modify affected cleartext traffic. Modified executable web content may also compromise the containing WebView session or exposed native interfaces.

entries.title: FileProvider Exposes Broad Filesystem Root
entries.remediation: Expose only dedicated app-owned sharing directories. Keep WebView file-origin and universal access disabled where possible, validate navigation, and issue narrowly scoped temporary file grants only to intended recipients.
entries.description: A file provider, plugin, or WebView permits access to a broad filesystem scope or relaxes file-origin isolation.
entries.impact: Untrusted content or a recipient with a usable file grant may read private files, disclose stored credentials, or access resources outside the directory intended for sharing.

entries.title: Weak Biometric Authentication Allowed
entries.remediation: Select the authenticator strength and freshness required by the operation. Bind sensitive keys to the intended authentication policy and invalidate them on enrollment changes when the threat model requires it.
entries.description: Biometric policy accepts a weaker authenticator, any enrolled biometric set, or a cached authentication result. Verify the protection required by the guarded operation.
entries.impact: A person who satisfies a weaker or previously cached authentication condition may unlock protected operations or keys without the user-presence or enrollment guarantees required by the application.

entries.title: Keystore Authentication Requirement Disabled
entries.remediation: Require user authentication for keys whose operations need user presence. Choose an appropriate authentication timeout and verify both key-generation parameters and the operation’s authorization policy.
entries.description: A keystore key explicitly disables the requirement for user authentication before use.
entries.impact: A process able to use the application’s key may perform protected cryptographic operations without confirming user presence, weakening controls intended to gate decryption or sensitive actions.

entries.title: Secure Window Protection Explicitly Cleared
entries.remediation: Protect sensitive screens where required by the threat model. Require clear user consent for capture, limit the captured content and retention, and keep captured images out of logs and unauthorized uploads.
entries.description: The checked code clears secure-window protection or invokes screen-capture APIs. Determine what content can be captured and how consent and resulting images are handled.
entries.impact: Captured screens may expose passwords, one-time codes, financial information, or private communications to capture recipients or insecure storage when sensitive content is included.

entries.title: Custom Permission Uses Weak Protection Level
entries.remediation: Disable external access when it is unnecessary. Otherwise use suitable signature permissions or explicit caller authorization, validate all incoming data, and test access from an untrusted application.
entries.description: An Android component or receiver exposes an entry point with a weak or unresolved caller permission boundary. Manifest merging and runtime authorization may affect the effective policy.
entries.impact: An unauthorized application may invoke exposed operations, read protected data, or change application state if no effective caller check protects the entry point.

entries.title: Code Shrinking Configuration Review
entries.remediation: Verify shrinking and obfuscation requirements against the final application release artifact. Keep secrets and trust decisions out of client code regardless of obfuscation.
entries.description: A build configuration disables code shrinking in a non-debug or unresolved scope. This does not establish the final application’s release configuration.
entries.impact: Disabled shrinking or obfuscation may make distributed code easier to inspect and increase retained attack surface; it does not create an access-control boundary or prove an exploitable vulnerability.

entries.title: Debug Task Entitlement Enabled
entries.remediation: Remove debug-task entitlements from distribution builds. Verify the final signed entitlement set and keep production authorization enforced independently of the client process.
entries.description: Apple application configuration enables the debug-task entitlement. Verify the entitlement in the signed distribution artifact.
entries.impact: An actor with the necessary device access may attach a debugger to the distributed application and inspect or alter its process, potentially exposing in-memory secrets or bypassing client-side checks.

entries.title: File Data Protection Explicitly Disabled
entries.description: Source explicitly selects a file protection option that does not restrict access when the device is locked. Identify the affected file and whether it contains sensitive information.
entries.impact: An actor with sufficient device or process access may read sensitive files while the device is locked if the selected protection class leaves their keys available. This does not mean the device stores all files unencrypted.
entries.remediation: Use an appropriate protected file class for sensitive content, accounting for background access requirements. Inspect the effective attributes on the shipped app’s files on a locked device.

entries.title: Keychain Synchronization Enabled
entries.description: A keychain query explicitly enables synchronization. Determine whether this operation creates or updates sensitive items or merely searches existing items.
entries.impact: Sensitive items created with synchronization enabled may be replicated beyond the current device. Exposure depends on the item operation, account security, and the application’s intended trust boundary.
entries.remediation: Keep device-bound secrets non-synchronizing when required by their threat model. Use suitable ThisDeviceOnly accessibility and authentication controls; verify the actual SecItemAdd or update operation.

entries.title: Keychain Access Control Allows Any Biometric Enrollment
entries.remediation: Select the authenticator strength and freshness required by the operation. Bind sensitive keys to the intended authentication policy and invalidate them on enrollment changes when the threat model requires it.
entries.description: Biometric policy accepts a weaker authenticator, any enrolled biometric set, or a cached authentication result. Verify the protection required by the guarded operation.
entries.impact: A person who satisfies a weaker or previously cached authentication condition may unlock protected operations or keys without the user-presence or enrollment guarantees required by the application.

entries.title: Application Documents Exposed Through File Sharing
entries.remediation: Disable document sharing when unnecessary. Keep secrets and private records outside the shared Documents directory and verify the distribution configuration and actual exposed files.
entries.description: Application configuration enables document-directory sharing. Identify the files exposed through this setting and whether sensitive records are stored there.
entries.impact: A person with access to the device’s file-sharing interface may copy exposed application documents. The risk depends on the files present and the applicable device access controls.

entries.remediation: Expose only dedicated app-owned sharing directories. Keep WebView file-origin and universal access disabled where possible, validate navigation, and issue narrowly scoped temporary file grants only to intended recipients.
entries.description: A file provider, plugin, or WebView permits access to a broad filesystem scope or relaxes file-origin isolation.
entries.impact: Untrusted content or a recipient with a usable file grant may read private files, disclose stored credentials, or access resources outside the directory intended for sharing.

entries.remediation: Remove or redact sensitive values before logging. Disable verbose payload and shell tracing in production, restrict log access, and rotate active credentials that have already been exposed.
entries.description: Diagnostic output or execution tracing includes values that may contain credentials, tokens, or private user data.
entries.impact: Sensitive values written to logs may be recovered by log readers, telemetry operators, or other parties with access to collected diagnostics, enabling account misuse or disclosure of private data.

entries.title: Legacy TLS Minimum Configured
entries.remediation: Require supported TLS versions for affected endpoints, remove unnecessary legacy exceptions, and verify negotiated protocols against the server configuration.
entries.description: Transport configuration permits a legacy minimum TLS protocol version.
entries.impact: Connections that negotiate an obsolete protocol may lose expected transport protections and become more susceptible to protocol-specific interception or tampering attacks.

entries.title: OkHttp Hostname Verifier Always Accepts
entries.remediation: Restore platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Reject invalid server trust, remove permissive callbacks and environment overrides from production, and use properly configured test trust stores for development.
entries.description: The checked code or configuration bypasses a certificate, hostname, or server-trust decision. Resolve the effective callback and build configuration before confirming a production bypass.
entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.

entries.title: Room Destructive Migration Enabled
entries.remediation: Use explicit tested migrations and controlled recovery for decryption failures. Preserve recoverable data, surface failures to the user, and require deliberate authorization before destructive reset.
entries.description: Storage configuration permits destructive reset when migration or decryption fails.
entries.impact: A failure or triggered reset may erase persisted user data or credentials and disrupt service. Actual data loss depends on whether the reset path is reachable and whether recovery is available.

entries.title: Sensitive Value Stored in SavedStateHandle
entries.remediation: Store credentials and cryptographic secrets in the platform’s secure credential or key store. Keep them out of preferences and saved-state snapshots, and minimize retained values and backup exposure.
entries.description: The application stores a potentially sensitive value in general-purpose preferences, saved state, or other storage not designed as a credential vault.
entries.impact: A party who can access saved state, backups, or application storage may recover the sensitive value and use exposed credentials or private data outside the intended security boundary.

entries.title: Alamofire Trust Evaluation Disabled

entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.

entries.title: Core Data Store Explicitly Disables File Protection
entries.remediation: Choose an appropriate platform file-protection class for sensitive data and apply it to the persistent store and related files. Verify protection after migration and backup or restore.
entries.description: A file or persistent store explicitly disables platform data protection.
entries.impact: Someone who obtains the stored files may recover private application data without the device-lock protection intended for those files, depending on the device state and available access.

entries.title: SwiftUI AppStorage Persists Sensitive Value

entries.impact: A party who can access saved state, backups, or application storage may recover the sensitive value and use exposed credentials or private data outside the intended security boundary.

entries.title: Sensitive Input Autocorrection Explicitly Enabled
entries.description: A potentially sensitive input explicitly enables autocorrection. Check secure-entry settings on the same field, since secure entry disables autocorrection and spelling behavior.
entries.impact: If secure entry is ineffective and the keyboard retains this input, secret text may enter keyboard learning or suggestion data and be exposed outside the intended field.
entries.remediation: Use secure entry for credentials and disable autocorrection and spell checking for other sensitive fields. Validate the effective settings and third-party keyboard behavior on a device.

entries.title: Dio Accepts Every HTTP Response Status
entries.remediation: Accept only the status codes expected by each operation. Handle authentication failures, redirects, and server errors explicitly before consuming response data or updating trusted state.
entries.description: The HTTP client accepts every response status as successful.
entries.impact: If callers treat rejected or failed responses as valid, they may make incorrect authorization or transaction decisions, process attacker-controlled error content, or conceal security-relevant failures.

entries.title: Hive Uses a Constant Encryption Key
entries.remediation: Keep encryption keys in an appropriate key-management facility and use modern authenticated encryption for confidential data. Migrate legacy ciphertext safely, with unique nonces and keys appropriate to the selected algorithm.
entries.description: The checked cryptographic configuration uses a constant embedded key, ECB mode, or a legacy algorithm. Establish whether the operation protects confidential or integrity-sensitive data.
entries.impact: Embedded keys can be recovered from distributed code, and unsuitable algorithms or ECB mode may expose plaintext relationships or weaken confidentiality. Consequences depend on key handling, data format, and the security purpose of the operation.

entries.title: Expo Update Safety Protections Disabled
entries.remediation: Keep update safety checks enabled, verify update authenticity and channel configuration, and test rollback behavior before distributing updates.
entries.description: The application disables a safety mechanism in its runtime update configuration.
entries.impact: If the disabled mechanism was preventing unsafe updates or launches, a bad or untrusted update may disrupt availability or replace trusted application behavior, depending on the remaining signing and update controls.

entries.title: Flutter Secure Storage Resets on Decryption Error
entries.remediation: Use explicit tested migrations and controlled recovery for decryption failures. Preserve recoverable data, surface failures to the user, and require deliberate authorization before destructive reset.
entries.description: Storage configuration permits destructive reset when migration or decryption fails.
entries.impact: A failure or triggered reset may erase persisted user data or credentials and disrupt service. Actual data loss depends on whether the reset path is reachable and whether recovery is available.

entries.title: Flutter Keychain Accessible After First Unlock
entries.remediation: Use a keychain accessibility class and synchronization policy appropriate to the secret. Prefer device-only and unlocked-device restrictions for secrets that require those boundaries; verify background-access requirements before changing them.
entries.description: Keychain configuration allows synchronization or access after the device’s first unlock. Compare the selected policy with the secret’s required device and lock-state boundaries.
entries.impact: Secrets may remain usable while the device is locked or become available on synchronized devices, expanding access beyond a policy that requires an unlocked device or device-only custody.

entries.title: Container Build Pipes Download Into Shell
entries.remediation: Fetch a pinned artifact through authenticated transport, verify its signature or checksum against a trusted source, and inspect it before execution. Avoid piping mutable remote content directly into a shell.
entries.description: The container build downloads content and pipes it directly to a shell.
entries.impact: Compromised or substituted download content may execute with build privileges, alter the resulting image, or extract build-time secrets.

entries.title: Cloud Instance Allows IMDSv1
entries.remediation: Require the token-based metadata protocol, restrict metadata access to required workloads, and assign the instance role only the permissions it needs.
entries.description: Cloud instance metadata configuration permits the legacy sessionless metadata protocol.
entries.impact: A reachable server-side request forgery or local process may obtain instance metadata or role credentials more easily when the metadata service does not require a session token.

entries.title: Kubernetes Service Account Token Automount Enabled
entries.remediation: Disable token automount for workloads that do not need the cluster API. For required access, use a narrowly privileged service account and short-lived projected tokens.
entries.description: A workload explicitly permits automatic mounting of a service-account token.
entries.impact: A compromised container may use the mounted token to call the cluster API with the service account’s permissions, potentially expanding compromise beyond the workload.

entries.title: Literal HTTP Basic Authorization Header
entries.remediation: Remove embedded credentials and load them from an approved secret store. Rotate exposed active credentials and restrict their privileges and lifetime.
entries.description: A connection URL or authorization header embeds credential material directly in the checked source.
entries.impact: Anyone who can read the source, build artifacts, or copied configuration may recover active credentials and access the associated service with the credential owner’s privileges.

entries.title: Mutable PendingIntent Capability
entries.description: Intent or PendingIntent configuration permits mutation, unsafe implicit delivery, or bypass of intent-redirection protection. Resolve the intended recipient and effective flags.
entries.remediation: Prefer explicit destinations and immutable PendingIntents. Where mutation is required, tightly constrain recipients and fill-in fields, validate nested intents, and retain platform redirection protections.
entries.impact: An untrusted recipient or input may redirect execution or alter an operation performed under the application’s identity if mutable fields or an implicit target cross a trust boundary.

entries.title: Runtime Broadcast Receiver Exported
entries.description: An Android component or receiver exposes an entry point with a weak or unresolved caller permission boundary. Manifest merging and runtime authorization may affect the effective policy.
entries.remediation: Disable external access when it is unnecessary. Otherwise use suitable signature permissions or explicit caller authorization, validate all incoming data, and test access from an untrusted application.
entries.impact: An unauthorized application may invoke exposed operations, read protected data, or change application state if no effective caller check protects the entry point.

entries.title: Intent URI Parsing Entry Point
entries.description: The application registers or parses an externally supplied URI or link. Registration alone does not establish unsafe routing or authorization.
entries.remediation: Allowlist accepted schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate link parameters, require authorization before sensitive actions, and verify domain association when relying on trusted web links.
entries.impact: A crafted link may trigger unauthorized actions, redirect navigation, or expose private data if the receiving handler trusts URI fields or bypasses authentication and object-level authorization.

entries.title: WebMessage Wildcard Origin
entries.description: An origin policy accepts a wildcard for browser requests or WebView messaging. Identify the resources or native operations accessible through this policy.
entries.remediation: Allow only the exact trusted origins required by the feature. Authenticate and authorize each operation independently; validate message origin and content before invoking native functionality.
entries.impact: An untrusted website may read protected responses or invoke privileged message handlers if the effective origin policy admits it and the resource or handler lacks the required independent access controls.

entries.title: WebView Safe Browsing Disabled

entries.remediation: Keep safe browsing enabled for externally reachable web content. Restrict navigation to required trusted destinations and handle unsafe-resource callbacks without bypassing warnings.
entries.impact: Users may be exposed to known malicious or phishing content without the platform’s warning or blocking layer when such content is loaded.

entries.title: World-Accessible Android Storage
entries.description: The application declares or uses broadly accessible storage. Resolve the actual directories, access mode, platform version, and sensitivity of stored data.
entries.remediation: Keep private data in app-private storage and use platform-scoped access for deliberate sharing. Authenticate or validate externally read files and avoid storing executable or credential material in shared locations.
entries.impact: Other actors with access to shared storage may read sensitive files or replace content later consumed by the application, compromising confidentiality or integrity.

entries.title: Shared External Storage Write Surface

entries.title: Android Raw SQL Review Surface
entries.positive: db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=" + intent.getStringExtra("id"), null)
entries.negative: db.query("users", columns, "id=?", arrayOf(id), null, null, null)
entries.description: The code invokes a raw SQL interface. The text match does not establish whether query structure is controlled by external data.
entries.remediation: Bind data values as parameters and allowlist dynamic identifiers. Trace query construction and validate object-level authorization for the records being accessed.
entries.impact: If untrusted values are concatenated into SQL syntax, an attacker may read or modify database records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges.

entries.title: WebView Native Bridge Review Surface
entries.description: The application exposes a native bridge or message handler to web content.
entries.remediation: Expose only narrowly required native methods. Restrict loaded origins and message senders, validate message schemas, and authorize every sensitive native action.
entries.impact: Untrusted web content may invoke native operations with the application’s privileges if origin restrictions, message validation, or per-operation authorization are missing.

entries.title: Dynamic Android Code Loading
entries.description: The code dynamically loads executable material or alters runtime method dispatch. Resolve the source, integrity checks, and intended use of that material.
entries.remediation: Load only approved code from trusted locations, verify integrity and authenticity before loading, and keep runtime hooks confined to documented, authorized behavior.
entries.impact: A party able to replace loaded code or control a runtime hook may execute with the application’s privileges, inspect private data, or alter security decisions. Legitimate bundled code and instrumentation do not establish an attack.

entries.title: Native Library Loading Review

entries.title: Android Shell Execution Review
entries.description: The checked code invokes a command or shell execution API. Trace command construction and argument values to determine whether external input can influence execution.
entries.remediation: Use a fixed executable and a separate argument array without a shell. Allowlist permitted operations and validate each argument according to the invoked program’s semantics.
entries.impact: If an attacker can alter executable selection or shell syntax, commands may run with the application’s privileges, exposing data, modifying files, or disrupting service.

entries.title: Accessibility Capture Or Automation Capability
entries.description: The application uses an accessibility or notification-access capability that can observe information or interact with other applications.
entries.remediation: Explain the capability clearly and require appropriate user authorization. Limit captured content and automated actions to the requested feature, minimize retention, and prevent unauthorized transmission.
entries.impact: Captured interface or notification content may disclose private messages, authentication codes, or user activity; automated actions may affect other applications if the capability is used beyond the user’s authorization.

entries.title: SMS Transmission Capability
entries.description: The application sends SMS messages or declares a capability to receive or inspect SMS content.
entries.remediation: Request only the SMS capabilities needed by a user-visible feature. Require explicit intent for sending, protect received message content, and prevent logs or unauthorized uploads of verification codes.
entries.impact: Unauthorized SMS handling may expose verification codes or private messages, cause unwanted messaging charges, or affect account recovery if the relevant permission and execution path are available.

entries.title: Notification Capture Capability

entries.title: Screen Capture Capability
entries.description: The checked code clears secure-window protection or invokes screen-capture APIs. Determine what content can be captured and how consent and resulting images are handled.
entries.remediation: Protect sensitive screens where required by the threat model. Require clear user consent for capture, limit the captured content and retention, and keep captured images out of logs and unauthorized uploads.
entries.impact: Captured screens may expose passwords, one-time codes, financial information, or private communications to capture recipients or insecure storage when sensitive content is included.

entries.title: Application Component Visibility Changed
entries.description: The application changes whether a component is enabled or visible to the user.
entries.remediation: Keep component visibility changes tied to documented user choices or application lifecycle needs. Preserve accessible settings and removal controls, and verify that changes cannot conceal unauthorized behavior.
entries.impact: Concealing an application entry point may reduce user visibility or interfere with access to controls if used without consent; the API itself does not establish malicious persistence or an authorization bypass.

entries.title: Package Installation Capability
entries.description: The application requests or uses package installation or broad package-discovery capabilities.
entries.remediation: Use scoped package queries and platform installation prompts. Require clear user intent for installation, verify the package source and integrity, and avoid collecting an unnecessary application inventory.
entries.impact: Unapproved installation may introduce executable software, and broad package discovery may reveal sensitive information about the user’s installed applications when consent or data-use controls are inadequate.

entries.title: Device Administrator Or Lock Control
entries.description: The code uses device-administrator or lock-control functionality.
entries.remediation: Use device-management privileges only for clearly authorized management features. Minimize requested policies and provide transparent activation, recovery, and deactivation behavior.
entries.impact: Misuse of an activated administrator capability may lock the device, alter device policy, or disrupt user access, depending on the privileges actually granted.

entries.title: Persistent Device Identifier Access
entries.description: The application accesses a persistent or advertising identifier, or declares tracking in its privacy configuration.
entries.remediation: Collect identifiers only for a justified, consented purpose. Prefer scoped resettable identifiers, respect tracking authorization and reset behavior, and minimize sharing and retention.
entries.impact: Linking identifiers to activity across sessions or services may expose a user’s behavior or enable unwanted tracking when collection and sharing exceed the user’s consent.

entries.description: A file provider, plugin, or WebView permits access to a broad filesystem scope or relaxes file-origin isolation.
entries.remediation: Expose only dedicated app-owned sharing directories. Keep WebView file-origin and universal access disabled where possible, validate navigation, and issue narrowly scoped temporary file grants only to intended recipients.
entries.impact: Untrusted content or a recipient with a usable file grant may read private files, disclose stored credentials, or access resources outside the directory intended for sharing.

entries.title: WKWebView App-Bound Navigation Disabled
entries.description: WebView configuration disables the app-bound navigation limit.
entries.remediation: Enable app-bound navigation where the feature requires it, restrict navigation destinations, and avoid exposing privileged scripts or native handlers to untrusted pages.
entries.impact: Untrusted navigation may expose a broader set of pages to privileged WebView functionality if application-bound restrictions were intended to isolate sensitive features.

entries.description: Biometric policy accepts a weaker authenticator, any enrolled biometric set, or a cached authentication result. Verify the protection required by the guarded operation.
entries.remediation: Select the authenticator strength and freshness required by the operation. Bind sensitive keys to the intended authentication policy and invalidate them on enrollment changes when the threat model requires it.
entries.impact: A person who satisfies a weaker or previously cached authentication condition may unlock protected operations or keys without the user-presence or enrollment guarantees required by the application.

entries.title: Cross-Application Pasteboard Read
entries.description: The application reads the shared clipboard or pasteboard. Review whether the read follows an explicit paste action and whether the returned content enters logs, storage, or network requests.
entries.remediation: Read clipboard content only for an explicit user paste action. Process only the value needed for that action, avoid logging or transmitting it unnecessarily, and respect platform clipboard access restrictions.
entries.impact: Passwords, payment details, or other private content copied from another application could be collected or disclosed if clipboard reads occur without user intent or the content is sent to an unauthorized recipient. Platform access restrictions and the actual handling of the data determine exposure.

entries.impact: Location records may reveal movements, home or work addresses, and personal routines if collection or sharing exceeds the authorized feature or stored history is exposed.

entries.impact: Sensitive keychain items may become accessible to other applications in the permitted group, expanding the credential trust boundary beyond a single application.

entries.impact: Private provider data may be disclosed or modified if the provider lacks effective caller authorization or if attacker-controlled selection text changes the intended query.

entries.title: WebView Universal File-Origin Access Enabled
entries.description: A file provider, plugin, or WebView permits access to a broad filesystem scope or relaxes file-origin isolation.
entries.remediation: Expose only dedicated app-owned sharing directories. Keep WebView file-origin and universal access disabled where possible, validate navigation, and issue narrowly scoped temporary file grants only to intended recipients.
entries.impact: Untrusted content or a recipient with a usable file grant may read private files, disclose stored credentials, or access resources outside the directory intended for sharing.

entries.title: Hardcoded Authentication Comparison
entries.description: Authentication-related code compares against a literal value. Determine whether it is a real credential check, a test fixture, or a non-secret state comparison.
entries.remediation: Remove embedded authentication secrets and enforce authentication through a trusted verifier. Rotate exposed active values and keep test-only bypasses out of release builds.
entries.impact: If a distributed constant acts as an authentication secret or grants privileged access, someone who recovers it may impersonate a user or bypass the intended authentication process.

entries.title: Server Trust Credential Override Surface
entries.description: The checked code or configuration bypasses a certificate, hostname, or server-trust decision. Resolve the effective callback and build configuration before confirming a production bypass.
entries.remediation: Restore platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Reject invalid server trust, remove permissive callbacks and environment overrides from production, and use properly configured test trust stores for development.
entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.

entries.title: Release WebView Inspection Enabled
entries.description: WebView remote debugging or inspection is explicitly enabled. Determine whether the setting reaches a distributed production build.
entries.remediation: Enable WebView inspection only in verified development builds. Disable it in distributed releases and verify the setting in the final application artifact.
entries.impact: A party with access to the platform’s debugging interface may inspect page content, extract session data, or execute scripts in the application’s WebView when production debugging remains accessible.

entries.title: SMS Interception Capability Declaration
entries.description: The application sends SMS messages or declares a capability to receive or inspect SMS content.
entries.remediation: Request only the SMS capabilities needed by a user-visible feature. Require explicit intent for sending, protect received message content, and prevent logs or unauthorized uploads of verification codes.
entries.impact: Unauthorized SMS handling may expose verification codes or private messages, cause unwanted messaging charges, or affect account recovery if the relevant permission and execution path are available.

entries.title: Package Installation Or Broad Enumeration Capability
entries.description: The application requests or uses package installation or broad package-discovery capabilities.
entries.remediation: Use scoped package queries and platform installation prompts. Require clear user intent for installation, verify the package source and integrity, and avoid collecting an unnecessary application inventory.
entries.impact: Unapproved installation may introduce executable software, and broad package discovery may reveal sensitive information about the user’s installed applications when consent or data-use controls are inadequate.

entries.title: Cross-Application Overlay Capability
entries.description: The application requests permission to draw over other applications.
entries.remediation: Use overlays only for a transparent user-authorized feature. Avoid sensitive input capture, make overlays dismissible, and honor platform restrictions on protected screens.
entries.impact: An authorized overlay may obscure trusted interface elements or imitate prompts, enabling misleading interactions or credential capture if the feature is misused.

entries.title: Background Persistence Capability Declaration
entries.description: The manifest declares background-service, boot, wake-lock, or related persistence capabilities.
entries.remediation: Limit background execution to justified tasks, provide required user-visible notifications and controls, and stop services and release wake locks when their work ends.
entries.impact: Unnecessary or undisclosed background activity may prolong data collection, consume device resources, or continue network activity beyond the user’s expected application lifecycle.

entries.title: Broad External Storage Capability
entries.description: The application declares or uses broadly accessible storage. Resolve the actual directories, access mode, platform version, and sensitivity of stored data.
entries.remediation: Keep private data in app-private storage and use platform-scoped access for deliberate sharing. Authenticate or validate externally read files and avoid storing executable or credential material in shared locations.
entries.impact: Other actors with access to shared storage may read sensitive files or replace content later consumed by the application, compromising confidentiality or integrity.

entries.title: Global ATS Arbitrary Loads
entries.description: The effective transport policy may permit insecure HTTP content or relax transport protections for a WebView, media request, domain, or application.
entries.remediation: Use HTTPS with normal certificate validation. Remove unnecessary transport exceptions, keep any unavoidable exception narrowly scoped, and avoid sending credentials or loading executable content over cleartext connections.
entries.impact: A network attacker may read or modify affected cleartext traffic. Modified executable web content may also compromise the containing WebView session or exposed native interfaces.

entries.title: Debug Task Entitlement In Apple Configuration
entries.description: Apple application configuration enables the debug-task entitlement. Verify the entitlement in the signed distribution artifact.
entries.remediation: Remove debug-task entitlements from distribution builds. Verify the final signed entitlement set and keep production authorization enforced independently of the client process.
entries.impact: An actor with the necessary device access may attach a debugger to the distributed application and inspect or alter its process, potentially exposing in-memory secrets or bypassing client-side checks.

entries.title: Documents Exposed To Other Applications
entries.description: Application configuration makes its document directory available through file sharing or document browsing.
entries.remediation: Keep credentials and private internal files outside shared document directories. Disable unnecessary sharing or expose only documents deliberately approved for external access.
entries.impact: Private files stored in the exposed directory may be read or copied outside the application’s intended access boundary by users or other applications with permitted document access.

entries.title: Android Runtime Method Hooking
entries.description: The code dynamically loads executable material or alters runtime method dispatch. Resolve the source, integrity checks, and intended use of that material.
entries.remediation: Load only approved code from trusted locations, verify integrity and authenticity before loading, and keep runtime hooks confined to documented, authorized behavior.
entries.impact: A party able to replace loaded code or control a runtime hook may execute with the application’s privileges, inspect private data, or alter security decisions. Legitimate bundled code and instrumentation do not establish an attack.

entries.title: Android Clipboard Read Capability
entries.description: The application reads the shared clipboard or pasteboard. Review whether the read follows an explicit paste action and whether the returned content enters logs, storage, or network requests.
entries.remediation: Read clipboard content only for an explicit user paste action. Process only the value needed for that action, avoid logging or transmitting it unnecessarily, and respect platform clipboard access restrictions.
entries.impact: Passwords, payment details, or other private content copied from another application could be collected or disclosed if clipboard reads occur without user intent or the content is sent to an unauthorized recipient. Platform access restrictions and the actual handling of the data determine exposure.

entries.title: Android Explicit ECB Or Legacy Cipher
entries.description: The checked cryptographic configuration uses a constant embedded key, ECB mode, or a legacy algorithm. Establish whether the operation protects confidential or integrity-sensitive data.
entries.remediation: Keep encryption keys in an appropriate key-management facility and use modern authenticated encryption for confidential data. Migrate legacy ciphertext safely, with unique nonces and keys appropriate to the selected algorithm.
entries.impact: Embedded keys can be recovered from distributed code, and unsuitable algorithms or ECB mode may expose plaintext relationships or weaken confidentiality. Consequences depend on key handling, data format, and the security purpose of the operation.

entries.title: Sensitive Text Input Explicitly Unmasked
entries.description: A text field whose identifier indicates secret input explicitly disables secure entry. Confirm the field’s content and whether an intentional reveal action limits this behavior.
entries.impact: An observer or recording mechanism may capture displayed credentials or secrets while the field is unmasked. Identifier matching alone does not establish that the field contains a secret.
entries.remediation: Enable secure entry for secret input by default. If a reveal feature is necessary, require explicit user intent and restore masking when the screen loses focus.

entries.title: TLS Peer Name Validation Disabled
entries.description: A stream SSL configuration explicitly disables the peer-name check. Verify the configuration is used by a reachable connection and inspect any independent hostname validation.
entries.impact: A network attacker with a certificate valid for another name may impersonate the expected endpoint if certificate-to-hostname matching is disabled without an equivalent check.
entries.remediation: Retain certificate chain validation and match the peer name to the intended host. Remove null peer-name overrides from production connection settings.

entries.title: Stream TLS Chain Validation Disabled
entries.description: A stream SSL configuration explicitly disables certificate-chain validation. Confirm the setting is applied to a network connection and whether equivalent trust validation exists.
entries.impact: A network attacker may use an untrusted certificate to intercept or modify traffic when the disabled platform check is not replaced with effective validation.
entries.remediation: Use platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Keep development trust exceptions isolated from distributed releases.

entries.title: Biometric Enrollment Key Invalidation Disabled
entries.description: A key policy explicitly disables invalidation after biometric enrollment changes. Verify biometric-only key authentication, credential fallback, key lifetime and applicable platform behavior.
entries.impact: A person able to enroll a new biometric may gain access to an existing protected key if the key’s effective policy accepts the new enrollment. This risk depends on authentication configuration.
entries.remediation: Invalidate biometric-bound keys when enrollment changes where the threat model requires it. Verify the effective key policy and use authenticated cryptographic operations for sensitive actions.

entries.title: Recent Tasks Screenshot Explicitly Enabled
entries.description: An activity explicitly allows screenshots for the recent-task preview. Determine whether sensitive content is visible and whether other window protections prevent capture.
entries.impact: Sensitive content visible during background transitions may appear in the task switcher when the effective window policy permits a preview.
entries.remediation: Disable recent-task screenshots for sensitive activities and apply the appropriate secure-window policy. Verify background transitions and screen recording on supported devices.

entries.title: WebView Content Provider Access Enabled
entries.description: WebView settings explicitly enable content-provider URL access. Identify loaded origins, provider permissions and whether untrusted content can request sensitive content URIs.
entries.impact: Untrusted content may access provider data reachable through the WebView when origin restrictions and provider controls are insufficient. Enabling this capability alone does not prove a data leak.
entries.remediation: Disable content access when unnecessary. Restrict loaded origins and provider access, and test content-URI reads from untrusted WebView pages.

entries.title: Sensitive Value Written To Preferences
entries.positive: SharedPreferences prefs = getSharedPreferences("user", MODE_PRIVATE); SharedPreferences.Editor editor = prefs.edit(); editor.putString("password", password);
entries.description: A preferences editor writes a value under a credential-related key. Resolve the actual backing store and whether the value is protected; MODE_PRIVATE restricts access but does not encrypt stored values.
entries.impact: If the stored value is a reusable unprotected credential, access to application files or permitted backups may expose it and allow unauthorized account use.
entries.remediation: Avoid retaining passwords. Use revocable session credentials with appropriate platform-backed protection, minimize retention and exclude secrets from backups.

entries.title: Verification Code Written To Console
entries.description: Verification-code data is passed directly to a console logging call.
entries.impact: Captured logs may disclose usable verification codes while they remain valid.
entries.remediation: Remove verification-code values from logs; test release logging and retention.

entries.title: Unencoded Address In Request Query
entries.description: A direct request template interpolates a raw variable into an address or search query value.
entries.impact: Delimiter characters may change query parameters and request meaning; destination control and SSRF are not established.
entries.remediation: Encode each query value with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent; validate endpoint-specific requirements.

entries.title: Camera Error Response Assets Not Checked
entries.description: An image-picker callback dereferences the first asset without a recognized local nonempty-assets guard.
entries.impact: An empty or error result may cause a local exception and disrupt the image operation.
entries.remediation: Handle cancellation and errors, require a nonempty assets array before indexing, and settle every operation outcome.

entries.title: Whole Redux State Persisted In Ordinary Storage
entries.description: An unrestricted ordinary-storage persistence configuration occurs alongside an authentication reducer declaration. This is file-level configuration review, not a proved stored-secret flow.
entries.impact: Sensitive authentication state may persist without appropriate protection if this configuration actually includes those fields.
entries.remediation: Resolve the persisted reducer and fields; exclude sensitive state or use protected storage, and verify logout and account switching.

entries.title: Placeholder Token Enters Authenticated UI
entries.description: A recognized sign-in or token-setting call receives a literal placeholder token.
entries.impact: Shipped prototype logic may enter a local authenticated state without verified credentials; server access is not established.
entries.remediation: Replace placeholder session values with a verified authentication result; exclude test and demonstration code from release behavior.

entries.title: Upload Limit Checks Only Current Batch
entries.description: A numeric limit checks only an incoming batch before a direct spread-based append to an existing collection.
entries.impact: Repeated additions may exceed the intended collection limit; receiving-service limits and actual resource impact remain unverified.
entries.remediation: Validate existing plus incoming count and decoded size; enforce applicable limits at the receiving service as well.

entries.title: Sensitive Value Written To PHP Log
entries.description: A PHP logging message directly includes a secret-like variable. Confirm the value, effective logging configuration, access and retention.
entries.impact: If the value holds an active password, token or key, readable logs may disclose credentials and permit access with their privileges.
entries.remediation: Remove passwords, tokens and secret keys from log messages. Use non-sensitive identifiers and verify release log access and retention.

entries.title: Embedded Datasource Password
entries.description: A datasource bean contains a literal password. Short passwords remain relevant. Configuration presence does not establish that the credential is active or deployed.
entries.impact: Readers of deployed source or configuration may recover the database credential and gain access with its effective privileges.
entries.remediation: Load database passwords from a restricted secret store. Rotate exposed active credentials and restrict the database account.
